newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt to sue Renault over closure procedure.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt to sue Renault over closure procedure.

text.p: The federal Belgian government and the government of the northern Flanders region will sue French car maker Renault over the procedure it followed in announcing the closure of its Belgian assembly plant, Belgian radio said on Monday.

BRTN radio quoted Flemish regional Economics Minister Eric Van Rompuy as saying Renault had breached Belgian and European Union rules on informing staff of and consulting staff on key company decisions.
A spokesman for Van Rompuy told Reuters, "We will take legal action. It has become clear that Renault did not observe a number of legal guidelines."
He said it was not entirely clear whether both governments would file suits. A working party made of representatives of both was to make the decision later on Monday.

BRTN quoted Van Rompuy as saying Renault had disregarded Belgian law and ignored the collective labour agreement for Renault Industrie Belgique, the car assembly unit in Vilvoorde near Brussels. It said Renault should have told Vilvoorde staff of the planned closure ahead of time.
Workers should have been asked for advice on the closure plan, it said.
Renault announced the surprise decision on Thursday, shocking the plant's 3,100 staff and at least 1,000 workers at suppliers and subcontractors.

BRTN said Van Rompuy spoke after meeting Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert of the European Commission, with whom he discussed the Renault Vilvoorde closure. Van Miert said unions could fight the closure before the courts.
BRTN said Renault also disregarded two European Union directives.
Van Miert said Renault management had failed to inform the group's European works council and disregarded EU guidelines on collective dismissals across borders.

"I do not understand the decision of Renault's management all too well because they are closing a very profitable plant in which they have invested a lot in recent years," he told BRTN earlier on Monday. "Actually I ask myself why this is happening while apparently elsewhere there are (plants) where it would be more appropriate."
He said the European Commission was "scandalised by this kind of behaviour."
